noAccess.title: No access to the dashboard
noAccess.body: Ask the clinic owner if you need it.

info.production: What visits charged in the period after discounts, by ledger date: charges with their corrections and reversals. A voided visit counts nothing. Opening balances and balance adjustments are not production.
info.collected: Payments received in the period minus refunds, by payment date. Voided payments never count; advances count when received.
info.collectionRate: Collected ÷ production. It passes 100% when patients pay old balances or in advance.
info.netResult: Collected − expenses. A cash view, not accounting: no accruals, depreciation or tax.
info.expenses: Confirmed expenses in the period, salaries, dentist payouts and lab payments included. Pending and voided ones never count.
info.receivables: What patients owe today, whatever the period.
info.discounts: Line and visit discounts on the visits charged in the period, with their share of the price before discounts.
info.average: Production ÷ the visits charged in the period. Voided visits are left out.
info.moneyInOut: The 12 months ending with the period. Hover a month for its net result and collection rate.
info.receivablesByAge: Unpaid charges by the age of each charge: the same buckets as Payments › Outstanding.
info.dentists: Production by the visit’s dentist; collections as the compensation statement counts them, when the payment is applied to the visit. Unallocated: collected that is not yet on any visit (credit, advances, old balances).
info.services: Production spread over each visit’s services; a correction moves it between them.
info.expensesByCategory: Each category’s share of what was collected in the period.
info.where: Each cost as a share of what was collected in the period.
info.methods: Collected by method, each refund taken from its own method.
info.planValue: Accepted treatment not started yet, by priority. Work in progress is already charged.
info.owes: Now, whatever the period: lab balances, salaries and dentist pay not paid yet, fixed expenses waiting at their usual amounts, and what patients hold as credit or advances.
info.visits: Visits finished in the period. Imported visits are history and never count here.
info.noShowRate: No-shows ÷ appointments due in the period (started by now). A rescheduled booking counts once, at its final time.
info.cancellationRate: Cancellations ÷ appointments due in the period.
info.newPatients: Patients whose first visit ever is in the period. A patient with an imported earlier visit is not new.
info.roomUse: Hours booked (not cancelled) ÷ opening hours × active rooms, over the days of the period that have passed. Dentist schedules do not exist yet.
info.wait: From check-in to the start of the visit, the same day. The share over 15 minutes is next to it.
info.planAcceptance: Of the plan items recorded in the period, the share the patient accepted.
info.activePatients: Patients with a visit in the last 12 months, whatever the period.
info.appointmentsByWeek: The 12 weeks ending with the period, by what became of each appointment due.
info.attention: Now, whatever the period. A line goes away when its count is zero.
info.busyHours: Appointments due in the period by weekday and starting hour. Darker is more.
info.treatmentPlans: Plan items recorded in the period, and the share that passed from the step before.
info.visitTypes: Finished visits by type: minutes booked on the appointment and minutes on the visit timer, on average.
info.dentistsOps: Each dentist’s visits, hours booked, average visit length, no-show rate, plan acceptance and median wait. Click a column to sort.
info.patients: New and returning patients per month. Came back: of patients first seen three to six months ago, the share with a later visit.
info.labs: From the lab reports: trips received on time, average turnaround against the lab’s promise, and remakes.
info.followUps: Follow-ups recommended in the period, and where they stand.
info.stock: Stock value now, each batch at what was paid for it, and what was taken out in the period at the cost of the batches it left, net of what was put back. The bars are the most consumed items by cost. Equal to Inventory’s Reports.
